title: 3Sum
description:
Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j`, `i != k`, `j != k`, and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`.

The solution set must not contain duplicate triplets. You may return the triplets, and the elements within each triplet, in any order.
hints: Sort the array first. Fixing the smallest element nums[i] turns the remaining problem into a sorted Two Sum with target -nums[i].
Use two pointers l = i + 1 and r = n - 1 that move inward depending on whether the current sum is less than, greater than, or equal to zero.
To avoid duplicate triplets without a hash set, skip repeated values of nums[i] and advance l and r past duplicate values after recording a valid triplet.

examples.explanation: The distinct triplets summing to 0 are [-1, -1, 2] and [-1, 0, 1].
The only triplet is [0, 1, 1], whose sum is 2 != 0.
The only possible triplet [0, 0, 0] sums to 0.
